## 1. B1, the claim

- Decidable after the fixes in 8. Fair as "how many", not as "which".
- BD 7.2 requires |A| ≠ |A′|, so the registered "Which" is a comparison of numbers by definition. Rename it "How many through made knots".
- Add the real one as a reported reading: **Which at equal number** (|A| = |A′|, A ≠ A′, courses differ). On a two-member Y with exchangeable members it is empty by symmetry; say so.
- Split B1 into three verdicts, each with its own minimal laws:
  - **B1-link**: a pair meets only through made knots.
  - **B1-ancestral**: one link is an ancestral common knot made by births.
  - **B1-dependence**: the course from X only differs, attributed through the meeting.
- The split matters because scratch item 1 already has 84 made-only meetings under recorded rations with MET-SOLE. The link needs no new ration; only the dependence does. Owner sentence 2 ("under the rules we had, it did not happen") is false for the meeting.
- The headline should be the made link, with the count said plainly in the same sentence. It bears on A241, where the dependence only replicates ticket A's kind of result.
- The sentence must say:
  - the rules added by hand (the sole take, the ration);
  - the starts and bounds;
  - that the link is one knot made in round 2 and a recorded ancestor of both parts;
  - that the difference is "both of Y's two members usable, against one or none";
  - the chain of the count (round-5 demand, round-6 owing, the offshoot's fresh count);
  - that it is not composed.
- It must not say: "reads", "which pattern", "in every numbering" (say "the law uses no names; checked on N renumberings"), "least" without "among the listed laws", or "first" without "in the record".
- Under FLOOR1 the round-5 demand fixes nothing the join holds. The count is handed one round later, as the owing, to an offshoot. RD 0's "the law hands a count over" names the demand; extend the wording.
- The scratch data suggest (unconfirmed) that X's count registers a Y birth that needs both members. Register a report of the Y-side knot in the extra demand group.

## 2. "Only through made knots"

- Register the strict form for the headline: the set of linking knots is nonempty and every one is made after round 0. Report FD 5.7's weaker class beside it.
- Define the empty case. A meeting by a take, or one linked only by newborns, has no linking knot under RD 3.5; "all made" is then vacuously true. Count the take's supplier as a link, or exclude the pair.
- "Ancestral common knot made by births" is derivable from FD 1.5 plus "made after round 0", but BD 4.1 changes it. BD quantifies over every member of X and Y, where FD speaks of the two members the knot is a common knot of. BD also drops "not the parent of both". Align it to FD 1.5 on the met members at the meeting round, and report the every-member form separately.
- First of its kind: only on the pre-registration's citation ("always a start knot"). The fold study's results are not among what I was shown. Made links under names existed (180 of 216), so the new things are "ancestral and made" and "no names".
- What would make it the start's after all; register each as a reported check:
  - a start knot holds a distinction through which the link meets X's or Y's descendants (report each linking distinction's origin round and holders);
  - a start knot enters the linking set in any barred run;
  - X and Y are images of one another under a symmetry of the start that fixes the link (all three starts with the case are rings with three loose each);
  - the link's ancestry back to the start, listed.
- Every made knot descends from start knots. The honest phrase is "the start supplies the ancestors; the knot and both parts are made".

## 3. PARENT-OWING against the premise

- It is on the allowed side of items 1 to 3 as written, but the test does not yet separate it from PARENT-LOOSE. Both hand a parent's count to a child.
- State the difference as a registered item: the handed value is not the quantity it sets. PARENT-LOOSE sets h from h, a mark kept down a descent; owing is formed anew from groups each round.
- Its plain form is "ORD with the parent's owing in place of the newborn's demand": f = max(o, 3 − p, 1). The drafted max(2, o) differs only for a taking offshoot with o ≤ 1. Register the plain form as a third control, or as the rule itself.
- PARENT-OWING-1 makes two-place offshoots, against SD lines 12–13. That is the likely cause of its failing knots under not-all-equal. It is a control, not a search member.
- Unbounded: a difference arriving at one birth under this ration is always one integer handed. "Handed in one value" is then true by implication, and the "more than v classes" test is empty. B1 here can be more than a count passed only by a composed case or a Which at equal number.
- A bounded version belongs in the search family, since it sits below in cost and "least" is wrong without it:
  - **PARENT-OWING-CAPk**, f = min(max(2, o), k), k = 3 and 4. By argument the seen case (7 against 6) vanishes; the base course also changes, so no prediction.
  - 2 + (o mod 2) as a marked comparison: does one bit suffice?
- `family.json` omits reader-test item 4 (what the rule changes with X alone) for every law.

## 4. B2, composed

- RD 4.4 is loose. An entry finer than P does not "induce P exactly", and a late entry inside X's own course can summarise everything.
- BD 7.3's "at least three classes" is wrong. Two classes over three patterns can be composed (an OR of two inputs). The drafter's "two classes, so it cannot be composed" is a bad inference; the conclusion holds only because one entry induces P.
- The test I would register:
  - The **input entries** are the entries of RD 3.3 whose differing part is classed through the meeting.
  - m is the least number of input entries, at distinct births, whose joint value refines P.
  - No difference: P has one class. Handed in one value: m = 1. Composed over several births: m ≥ 2.
  - Report m and the births.
- For a law with at most v values at a birth, "more than v classes" implies m ≥ 2. Keep it as a consistency check, not the definition.
- "Equal on every value through round t, different after" is only a later first difference (Lemma L). It is not a test of composition.
- Class C varies one number a. A composed verdict there would be two thresholds of one count. It can show that and nothing the owner means.
- The smallest class worth having is two by two: two independent features of the second pattern reaching X at different births. Examples: two second parts each barred or not, or a Y whose members are not exchangeable.
- That class needs a planted composed case, which this draft lacks. Make it a later ticket. Here, keep only the m reading on class M's subsets, which costs nothing.

## 5. The family, the order, "least"

- The count of 60 checks. The order is usable once these are fixed:
  - Define the order on "values": 1 < 2 < 3 < h(u) + 1 < unbounded, and say how a law combines its rules' values.
  - MET-SOLE is marked "recorded" with `new_rule: false`. It is new; mark it.
  - OFFSHOOT-TWO and PARENT-OWING-1 are in the search in `family.json` and "never in the search" in BD 2. Move them out. Otherwise PARENT-OWING-1 enters the minimal set under parity at equal cost.
  - SHORT-BY's "values" counts acts, not a newborn's holdings. Define item 5 for treatments.
- Incomplete for "least": no Q-SOLE (one holder step, below MET-SOLE) and no bounded owing. Add the CAPk laws. For Q-SOLE, add it or say "least among the listed laws".
- There to get a positive: the floor of two, tuned to the knot test. The plain form in 3 answers that.
- Cut the 18 marked comparisons, or run them last. Run STEPS2-SOLE last; it is above MET-SOLE in cost and showed no meeting. Cut class C.

## 6. Controls and catches

Not enough. Untested:
- **Alike by construction.** Add one start without the ring's symmetry (SD's seven-knot generator, or a ring with one knot holding four). No prediction. Until then the sentence says "two like parts".
- **Number only.** True on what was seen. Say "whether both", and report Which at equal number.
- **Lasting is implied.** Under RELEASE a lone member's offshoots multiply any difference in usable loose counts. Argue it and take it out of the headline, or replace it later with "a part from X only returns in one run and not the other".
- **Near the bounds.** The registered bound is 7 rounds. The difference is at round 6 and scratch lasting used rounds 7 and 8. As registered, k = 2 is not what was seen. Run the lasting reruns to round t_d + 2 whatever the main bound; they are small.
- **The guard.** If no limit is reached at ×1, the ×10 and ×100 runs are identical by construction. Run P2 only where the guard stopped, and record each run's peak counts.
- **A constant other than two** (an offshoot receives 3), to rule out "larger offshoots" alone.
- **The meeting in the one-member run.** BD 7.2 needs a made-only meeting in both runs. If the one-member run has no meeting, the registered reading fails on its own terms. Unchecked.

- **Lasting.** Which rounds, the knot test on the reruns, and a stop by the knot bound.
- **PARENT-OWING.**
  - o counts groups before cancellation.
  - Say that IMPLIED goes first.
  - A taking offshoot (p = 2) still receives max(2, o).
  - RELEASE offshoots of a member with cancelled groups.

  - o − h ≥ h equals CANCEL-OFFSHOOT.
  - The keeper stays in the demand roster with what it holds.
  - Whether it is short again in the next round.

## 11. Words and honesty

- Owner sentence 1 uses "carries", which RD 0 bars. It also uses "meet again", which FD keeps for the owner's own words.
- "Parts given off by one start": SD's "gives parts off" belongs to a part that returns.
- "Which through made knots" for a number (see 1).
- "In every numbering", "least", "it did not happen" and "first" each say more than 7 starts, 7 rounds and 60 laws can.
- The title says "read"; the body does not. Leave the ID and say it once.
- No sentence in the body says a pattern reads where the law hands a count over.

## 12. Sentences for the owner

- **Made link confirmed, a count through it.** "Two parts the growth made, on three ring starts, come to meet through one knot the growth itself made in round 2, which both descend from. No start knot links them, and the rule that does it uses no names. Such meetings already happen under the old rations. For one part's course to change with the other, we added one rule by hand: an offshoot receives as many fresh distinctions as its parent had groups. What then passes is one count, whether both of the other part's two members were usable. So the law handed a count over through a made knot; no pattern read anything, and nothing was composed over several births. Checked on N renumberings, 7 rounds, the listed laws only."
- **Not confirmed.** "Written afresh from the frozen text, the made link (or the dependence through it; say which) was not found: among n laws decided, none, m undecided. The scratch case failed at [the linking knots / attribution / a knot]. A241 stands as recorded: every knot both descend from is still a start knot."
- **A composed case found.** "Under [law], the first part's course separates second patterns that no single value at one of its births separates; it takes m births. This is the first difference not handed in one value. It is on [start] and [bars], which are supplied; it is not yet a fold of emergence."
